title: Using artificial intelligence and computer vision to detect and monitor unhealthy child-directed food and beverage marketing: a data-driven study.
summary: The study builds image classifiers and object detection on 8,283 manually labelled package images, then applies the learned workflow to Canadian breakfast cereals (n=1,765). The reported result is an AI-assisted inventory: 39.2% were classified as displaying child-directed marketing and 89.5% of these were assessed as restricted by the proposed nutrient-profile rules. These are model-inferred labels and hypothetical policy classification, not legal determinations or health effects.
ai_technology: Image classifiers and YOLO object detection identify child-directed marketing features on food packages.
